title: Customized, production ready inference with open source models: Dmytro (Dima) Dzhulgakov
talk_summary: A Fireworks AI founder pitches serving open-source models with a custom stack, arguing that smaller/fine-tuned models beat big proprietary ones on latency and cost for narrow domains. The actionable core is LoRA multi-tenant serving (thousands of adapters on one GPU, serverless per-token pricing) and tuning serving config to a latency constraint rather than raw throughput.

takeaways.technique: Multi-LoRA adapter serving on shared GPUs
takeaways.what_they_do: Serve many fine-tuned LoRA variants on the same GPU so per-variant fixed cost disappears and you still pay per token.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can do uh smart tricks and deploy multiple plur models on the same GPU uh actually thousands of them
takeaways.numbers: thousands of model variants on one GPU

takeaways.technique: Optimize for min cost under a latency SLO, not max throughput
takeaways.what_they_do: Frame serving config as minimizing cost subject to a latency constraint, then tune batching/settings to that cutoff.
takeaways.evidence_quote: think about Max like minimizing cost under a particular latency constraint
takeaways.numbers: multiple times higher throughput at fixed latency

takeaways.technique: Small specialized model for function-calling/agent loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Ship models fine-tuned specifically for function calling with structured/JSON grammar output, claiming comparable quality to big models at far lower latency.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you get similar performance from F tune Lama 3 at 10x speed
takeaways.numbers: up to 10x faster; ~10x speed on function-calling benchmarks

takeaways.technique: Structured generation via JSON grammar mode
takeaways.what_they_do: Constrain model output with a JSON schema/grammar so tool calls and structured responses are valid by construction.
takeaways.evidence_quote: structure generation uh with like with Json model grammar mode

takeaways.what_they_do: Cite narrow-domain benchmarks (function calling) showing a small tuned model matches a big one, as the basis for model choice.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for some of the function calling use cases like externally Benchmark from uh from Berkeley
